title: Advantages and Limitations of FastAPI
subtopics: Choosing the right tool for a project
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of advantages and limitations of fastapi in a FastAPI application.
Apply or interpret one example related to type-driven development.
Identify one limitation or failure case and describe how to verify it.

content.intro: This lesson covers advantages and limitations of fastapi within introduction to fastapi. Use the supplied syllabus topics as the coverage checklist, then connect them to the worked example and the verification task.
content.why_it_matters: You will use advantages and limitations of fastapi to build APIs whose contracts and behavior are understandable to both clients and maintainers. The practical aim is predictable client-server contracts, resource naming, typed parameters and correct HTTP semantics.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Advantages and Limitations of FastAPI matters because it is part of introduction to fastapi. In practice, focus on predictable client-server contracts, resource naming, typed parameters and correct HTTP semantics. A framework feature only helps when its assumptions match the application; keep input validation, business policy and side effects distinguishable.

items.title: Type-driven development
items.text: Use type-driven development as a design decision rather than a keyword to memorize. State the input and expected result, identify the boundary conditions, and connect the concept to the surrounding FastAPI request lifecycle.

items.title: Automatic validation and documentation
items.text: For automatic validation and documentation, define the accepted shape and constraints explicitly. Validate untrusted input at the boundary, distinguish omitted values from explicit nulls, and return only fields the caller is allowed to see.

items.title: Asynchronous request handling
items.text: For asynchronous request handling, identify which operation waits on I/O, which resources remain open, and what happens on timeout or disconnect. Async syntax does not make CPU-bound work faster or durable background jobs reliable by itself.

items.title: Ecosystem and deployment considerations
items.text: For ecosystem and deployment considerations, collect measurable evidence from a local or staging environment. Keep configuration environment-specific, avoid logging secrets, establish a rollback path, and do not claim performance or availability without measurements.

content_blocks.title: Worked example: Advantages and Limitations of FastAPI
content_blocks.code:
import asyncio

async def fetch_one(name: str) -> str:
    await asyncio.sleep(0)  # stand-in for non-blocking I/O
    return name

async def main():
    results = await asyncio.gather(fetch_one("A"), fetch_one("B"))
    print(results)
content_blocks.run_instructions: Run with asyncio.run(main()) in a standalone Python script. Async helps I/O concurrency; it does not make CPU-heavy code automatically faster.
content_blocks.reset_steps: For read-only examples, no reset is needed. For any example that writes state, use a disposable local database/test fixture; record the starting state and clean up only lab data. Never use production credentials or real personal data.

content_blocks.text: Adapt the example to cover “Type-driven development”. Write down the expected success result and one invalid, missing, duplicate, timeout or permission-boundary case that matters for this topic.

hints: Start with “Type-driven development” and state the required inputs, output and assumptions.
Change one thing at a time; check the official reference and capture the actual response/error instead of guessing.
Include a negative/edge-case check and document which behavior remains untested.
expected_output: A reviewable example or design note for Advantages and Limitations of FastAPI, covering the PDF subtopics, expected behavior and at least one verification check.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a code fragment without checking its assumptions.
common_mistakes.why: Installed versions, imported types, application structure and external services affect behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: State assumptions; check the versioned official docs; run a minimal local test and add one failure case.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating one happy-path response as proof of correctness.
common_mistakes.why: Invalid input, permissions, concurrency, timeouts and cleanup are not exercised by a single request.
common_mistakes.fix: Add focused normal and negative tests and record exact expected status/body.

common_mistakes.why: Even short examples may mutate records, reveal data or affect availability.
common_mistakes.fix: Use synthetic inputs and a disposable environment; review security, cleanup and rollback before promotion.
